technical.clientSecretHandling: Web apps send client_id and client_secret as form fields (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) to the token endpoint. Never put the secret in a URL or query string. PKCE without a secret is native-only, on a separate native-pkce endpoint that LinkedIn must enable for your app.

refreshTokens.notes: Programmatic refresh tokens are limited to approved Marketing Developer Platform partners, so a Share on LinkedIn app shouldn't expect a refresh_token. The documented path is to send the member through authorization again: if they are still signed in to LinkedIn and the token hasn't expired, the consent screen is skipped. For partners, refresh tokens last 365 days and are not extended when used.

redirectUriRules: Must match one of the redirect URLs registered on the app's Auth tab
Query parameters are ignored when matching; URLs containing # are invalid
Native PKCE apps may only use loopback IPs (http(s)://127.0.0.1:{port} or http(s)://[::1]:{port})
Whether http://localhost works for the standard web flow is not documented

profiles.intent: Post on behalf of members (any LinkedIn member posting to their own profile)

scopes.name: openid
scopes.purpose: Turns on Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect and returns an ID token

scopes.name: profile
scopes.purpose: Member's name and photo, plus the sub identifier from /v2/userinfo used to build the post author

scopes.name: email
scopes.purpose: Optional: the member's primary email (may be missing from responses)

scopes.name: w_member_social
scopes.purpose: Create, comment on and like posts as the signed-in member (granted by the Share on LinkedIn product)

testModeLimits.text: No development mode or user cap is documented for Share on LinkedIn. The limits that apply are 150 requests per member per day and 100,000 per app per day.

configGotchas.text: Every app is tied to a LinkedIn Page at creation, and you can never move it to another Page.
Requesting a different scope set invalidates all of a member's earlier tokens.
Posts API calls fail without a LinkedIn-Version header (YYYYMM), and also fail with a sunset version.

stage1.summary: Self-serve. You need a LinkedIn Page for the app, then you add the two open products and complete one code flow. The only wait is a Page super admin approving the app, and that is immediate if the super admin is you.

time.range: Under an hour if you are the Page's super admin

stage2.summary: w_member_social is an open permission. No app review, partner program or legal entity is documented for it, and Share on LinkedIn has no user cap. What limits production is the 60-day token with no refresh token, per-member daily rate limits, and an API Terms clause against automating posting.

stage1DoneWhen.text: GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo with your bearer token returns 200 with a sub. Then POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts with author urn:li:person:{sub}, X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0 and a current LinkedIn-Version header returns 201 with the post URN in x-restli-id.

blockedBy.how: A super admin of the LinkedIn Page you pick has 30 days to approve or deny associating your app with it, and also approves the separate Verify request. This is your own Page's admin, not each end user's.
LinkedIn can suspend or end API access at any time. Its API Terms forbid using the APIs to automate posting, and an over-limit app gets 429 until the daily reset.
Without a refresh token you must bring every member back through authorization before their 60 days run out. You also have to keep the LinkedIn-Version header on a version that hasn't been sunset.

profiles.bottomLine: Member posting is self-serve, and its permissions are open to all developers. The Community Management requirements (legal entity, screencast, vetting) don't apply. The real work is keeping members connected: tokens last 60 days with no refresh token, and the API Terms forbid automating posting.
topRisks: No refresh token for non-partners, so every member must re-authorize within 60 days
API Terms 3.1(26) prohibits using the APIs to automate posting, which matters for agent-driven posting
The app is permanently tied to the LinkedIn Page chosen at creation

steps.title: Pick or create the LinkedIn Page the app will belong to
instructions: Decide which LinkedIn Page will publish the app. The create form has a required-looking LinkedIn Page field and offers Create a new LinkedIn Page if you have none.
Choose carefully: an app can never be transferred to another Page. A merger, rebrand or lost Page access means creating new apps.
If you aren't a super admin of that Page, find out who is. They must approve the association within 30 days.

links.label: Associate an app with a LinkedIn Page

steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Portal
instructions: Sign in at https://www.linkedin.com/developers/apps (My apps) and click Create app.
On Create an app, fill in App name, LinkedIn Page (Page name or URL), and Privacy policy URL.
Click Upload a logo. Members see this image on the consent screen. The file has to be local; size and format rules were not found in official docs.
Don't put LinkedIn or Microsoft names or logos in the app name or logo.
Tick I have read and agree to these terms, then click Create app. The app appears under My apps.

links.label: Create a new app for a LinkedIn Page

steps.title: Get the Page super admin to verify the app
instructions: On the app's Settings tab, click Verify, then Generate URL in the Verify company dialog.
Click Copy URL, send the link to the Page super admin by email or LinkedIn message, then click I'm done.
The super admin opens the link, signs in and approves or denies. The link lasts 30 days, and a denial invalidates every link generated for the app.
Verification is required only for some products, but it's cheap and some products need it, so do it early.

steps.title: Add Share on LinkedIn and Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect
instructions: Open the app's Products tab.
Add Share on LinkedIn, which grants w_member_social.
Add Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect, which grants openid, profile and email.
Accept any product terms shown. Both products are granted at once with no review queue.
Do not add Community Management API to this app. It's a separate vetted product and can't share an app with other products.

steps.title: Register the redirect URL on the Auth tab
instructions: Open the app's Auth tab and add your callback under redirect URLs.
Use an absolute HTTPS URL with no #fragment. Query parameters are ignored when matching.
For Postman testing, use https://oauth.pstmn.io/v1/callback.
Check that the Auth tab lists openid, profile, email and w_member_social. Those are the only scopes you can request.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
instructions: On the Auth tab, copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
Keep the secret on your server or in a secret manager. Never put it in a URL or query string, or post it in forums.

steps.title: Send the member through the authorization URL
instructions: Open https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization?response_type=code&client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_URL&state=RANDOM&scope=openid%20profile%20email%20w_member_social
The member must accept all requested scopes; they can't pick a subset. Request only what you need.
The member signs in (password, Google, Apple or passkey on desktop and Android web) and clicks Allow.
LinkedIn redirects with code and state. Reject the response if state doesn't match. If the member cancels, you get error=user_cancelled_login or user_cancelled_authorize instead.
Sign in as the member who will post. The token belongs to whoever authorizes, not to the app owner.

steps.title: Exchange the code for an access token
instructions: Within 30 minutes, POST to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
Send grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret and the same redirect_uri.
Store access_token (allow up to 1000 characters) and expires_in, which is 60 days. Expect no refresh_token unless LinkedIn has enabled programmatic refresh for your app.

steps.title: Read the member id and publish a test post
instructions: GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo with Authorization: Bearer TOKEN. Expect 200 with sub, name and, optionally, email.
POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts with headers X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0, Linkedin-Version: YYYYMM (a version not yet sunset) and Content-Type: application/json.

Body: author urn:li:person:{sub}, commentary, visibility, distribution.feedDistribution MAIN_FEED, and lifecycleState PUBLISHED. Use CONNECTIONS visibility if the test shouldn't be public (CONNECTIONS is documented for ugcPosts; not checked against the Posts schema).
Expect 201 with the post URN in the x-restli-id header. Clean up with DELETE https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts/{encoded URN}, which returns 204.

links.label: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect

steps.title: Check your posting flow against the API Terms
instructions: API Terms 3.1(26) prohibits using the APIs to automate posting on LinkedIn. Design the flow so each post comes from a member's own action, and get a legal reading if an agent posts on a schedule.
Pre-filled post text needs a clear notice and must stay editable by the member (3.1(4)).
Get valid consent before accessing a member's content (5.2).

steps.title: Plan for re-authorization every 60 days
instructions: Track each member's expires_in and send them back through authorization before it runs out.
If the member is still signed in to LinkedIn and the token hasn't expired, LinkedIn skips the consent screen and redirects straight back.
Handle 401 by restarting authorization. Tokens also die on revocation, on a scope change, or when a newer flow issues a token.

steps.title: Pin and maintain the LinkedIn-Version header
instructions: Send a LinkedIn-Version header on every /rest call. The latest version is not applied by default, and a missing header returns an error.
Versions ship monthly and are supported for at least a year. Move to a newer one before yours is sunset (202511 sunsets on 2026-11-16).

steps.title: Watch rate limits in the Analytics tab
instructions: The Share on LinkedIn docs list 150 requests per member and 100,000 per app per day, resetting at midnight UTC.
Standard per-endpoint limits aren't published. Make one call to an endpoint, then read its limit on the app's Analytics tab.
Developer admins get an email, 1 to 2 hours late, when the app passes 75% of an app-level quota. Member-level breaches send no email.

blockers.fix: Back off until the midnight UTC reset and check the Analytics tab

blockers.cause: A flow requested a different scope set, which invalidates earlier tokens
blockers.fix: Request one consistent scope set everywhere

nuances.text: Posting as a member (Share on LinkedIn, w_member_social) is an open, self-serve permission. Posting as an organization (w_organization_social, Community Management API) is a separate product. It requires a registered legal organization, a verified business email, a Page-verified app, and a screencast plus test credentials for the Standard tier.
For Community Management, a rejected app can't re-apply; create a new app and submit a new Development tier request. Share on LinkedIn has no review.
Use POST /rest/posts with a LinkedIn-Version header for new code. /v2/ugcPosts still works but is being replaced; no sunset date is set.

The 3-legged OAuth page's sample request still uses legacy scopes (liteprofile, emailaddress), and its Step 4 calls /v2/me. For OpenID Connect apps, use openid profile email and read identity from /v2/userinfo.
Request openid even though it isn't in the open-permissions table; it's required for an ID token.
Build the post author as urn:li:person:{sub}. The discovery document declares pairwise subjects, so test this (untested here).

PKCE is documented only for native apps. It uses a separate endpoint (/oauth/native-pkce/authorization), loopback redirect URIs and S256, and LinkedIn must enable it for your app on request. Web apps use the client secret.
Programmatic refresh tokens are for approved partners only; a Share on LinkedIn-only app shouldn't count on one.

Two separate Page admin approvals exist: associating the app with a Page (super admin, within 30 days) and Verify (a Settings-tab request approved via a generated link). Verify is required mainly for Community Management.
The Developer Portal's Token Generator can mint a test token for your own account without writing the code flow, and the Token Inspector shows a token's TTL and scopes.
LinkedIn may interrupt consent with a security checkpoint, such as an email verification. Native apps must use the system browser, not a webview.
